title: Your first shift
hook: Nine trains, three tracks, nothing fails. Your timetable, your panel: get them all through on time.
text: 08:00 to 08:40 in the signal box of Bf Neustadt, alone and with nothing going wrong: the place to learn the panel. Choose a start signal in the picture, then its destination: the interlocking moves the points, locks the route and clears the signal. The dispatcher shows you the first trains; then you work by the timetable, and the dispatcher calls only when something does not go to plan. Regional trains meet at the island platform, and the intercity wants to pass the freight train. Nobody else is seated; no signal fails.

story.say: Morning! Your timetable shows every train with its track and times. First is RB 31 from Bergheim, for G2: tap signal A, on the table or in the panel, then the route to G2.
RB 32 comes from Talsee: signal F, route to G3. The two meet at platform 2 so that passengers can change: that is what the timetable's notes say.
A train leaves by a route too: N2 lets RB 31 out to Talsee, P3 lets RB 32 out to Bergheim. Let them go at their time in the Dep column, not before.
That is the whole craft. From here on the timetable is yours; mind its notes: GZ 47 waits in G3 until IC 2045 has passed on G1. I call only when something does not go to plan.
{train} is standing at signal {signal}. Set its route into {track}, please: every minute it waits there, it loses.
{train} should have left at {time} and is still at signal {signal}. Set its route out, please.
{train} is going to {track}; the timetable has it on {plan}. Mind the trains after it, and the passengers who change.
{train} has left before the passengers of {feeder} could change. A connection is worth a minute or two of waiting.

debrief: Which train did you let wait, and for which other train? Would you decide the same again?
A route is locked until the train has passed. What did that mean for the next train you wanted to let in?
The intercity and the freight train: where did you let one pass the other, and what did it cost the slower one?
